channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Ministro defende projeto do governo pelo fim da escala 6x1 e diz que reduzir para 36 horas é 'irresponsabilidade'
item.description: Labor Minister Luiz Marinho defended the government's bill to end the 6x1 work scale, stating that an immediate reduction to 36 weekly hours would be irresponsible. He argued that Brazil's economy can sustain a more gradual reduction to 40 hours per week, as proposed by the executive.

item.title: Não aceitarei “inversão de papéis”, diz Gaspar sobre Lindbergh e Soraya
item.description: Deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) rejected accusations of slander, defamation, and injuria from Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) and Soraya Thronicke (PSB-MS), claiming he is the victim of an unproven serious accusation. He denied committing rape of a vulnerable person and said the charges aim to discredit his INSS CPMI report. Gaspar said he will respond to the STF with concrete evidence and hopes the Ethics Committees of the Chamber and Senate will review his requests for the impeachment of his accusers.

item.title: Fachin diz que Judiciário vive crise e defende autocontenção do STF
item.description: STF President Edson Fachin stated that the Judiciary is facing a crisis and requires self-restraint and critical reflection on its limits. He emphasized that expansions of power must be accompanied by limits to avoid inadequate solutions for new problems. Fachin also highlighted the importance of using legal mechanisms, such as appeals, rather than attacking institutionality during disagreements.

item.title: Assessor de Marçal que agrediu marqueteiro grava vídeo com Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Nahuel Medina, an aide to Pablo Marçal who assaulted marketer Duda Lima in 2024, posted a video with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a presidential pre-candidate. Lima, a marketer for the Liberal Party, has seen his circle express outrage over the association, according to O Antagonista. The incident rekindles tensions between Marçal’s allies and Bolsonaro-aligned figures.

item.title: Bolsa Família volta a crescer e encosta nos 19 milhões de pagamentos
item.description: The Bolsa Família program reached 19 million payments in April 2026, recovering from a 2025 decline, though the average benefit per family dropped to R$678.22. Despite the rise in beneficiaries, total spending remained stable at R$12.8 billion due to the lower average payment. Experts suggest possible fraud, such as spouse omission and informal work to retain benefits, with 895,000 families receiving more in aid than from formal employment.

item.title: Girão defende reação do Senado contra atos do STF
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE) defended in the Senate plenary the need for greater initiative by the House regarding STF decisions, stating the Senate faces difficulties exercising its prerogatives and denouncing legal insecurity in the country. He criticized STF ministers, especially Gilmar Mendes, for requesting an investigation against Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) following his report in the Organized Crime CPI, alleging abuse of authority, and called the episode an attack on parliamentary immunity. Girão stated the Senate must admit the first impeachment process against an STF minister to prevent the 'togato dictatorship' and restore balance among the Powers.

item.title: Quase senador e sonho de Presidência: a decepção de Oscar Schmidt com a política
item.description: Oscar Schmidt, Brazilian basketball legend known as 'Mão Santa', died at age 66 on Friday. Beyond his sports career, he had a brief political stint in the 1990s, serving as municipal secretary of Sports in São Paulo and running for Senate under the PPB in 1998, where he placed second with over 5.7 million votes, losing to Eduardo Suplicy. Despite aspiring to the presidency, Schmidt became disillusioned with politics and withdrew from public life, stating in a 2024 interview that he was 'grateful to God' for not being elected.

item.title: Por Dentro das Eleições: Brasil utiliza sistemas eleitorais majoritário e proporcional
item.description: Brazil uses a mixed electoral system for the 2026 elections: majoritarian for executive offices (president, governor, mayor) and the Senate, and proportional for federal, state, district deputies and city council members. In majoritarian races, the candidate with the most votes wins (simple or absolute majority). In proportional representation, seats are allocated based on the total votes received by each party or federation, favoring the highest-voted candidates within each list.

item.title: Médicos indicam a possibilidade de mais uma cirurgia em Bolsonaro
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro's medical team told Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes that the former president is fit for surgery on his right shoulder, citing persistent pain during movement. Bolsonaro is currently under temporary house arrest following hospitalization for bilateral bacterial pneumonia due to bronchoaspiration, which had put his life at risk. The medical report was submitted to the STF as part of the review process for the precautionary measure, set to be reassessed in June.

item.title: STF tem maioria para manter decisão do TSE que cassou Rodrigo Bacellar
item.description: The First Chamber of the STF formed a majority to deny the appeal and uphold the removal and ineligibility of former Alerj president Rodrigo Bacellar, confirming the TSE's decision. Rapporteur Cristiano Zanin was joined by Alexandre de Moraes and Flávio Dino, with only Minister Cármen Lúcia's vote pending until April 28. The ruling deemed the appeal premature, as the TSE's full court may still review the decision.

item.title: Flávio diz que Moraes vai usar o STF para desequilibrar as eleições
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) accused Minister Alexandre de Moraes of using his position at the STF to interfere in the 2026 elections, claiming the inquiry opened against him for slander against Lula is part of a strategy to unbalance the race and silence right-wing opponents. He stated that the 'fake news' inquiry, opened seven years ago, will be repeatedly used during the campaign to restrict his freedom of speech. Senate President Rodrigo Pacheco (misidentified as 'Alcolumbre' in the text) offered legal support to senators to defend the legitimacy of the vote and parliamentary prerogatives.

item.title: Como a capital de JK se tornou centro da tecnologia eleitoral e o futuro da democracia
item.description: Brasília, Brazil's capital founded 66 years ago, has become the nation's electoral technology hub by hosting the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), which designed, tested, and validated the electronic voting system now recognized globally for its transparency and auditability. As a symbol of Brazilian modernity since the Juscelino Kubitschek era, the city now serves as the 'central nervous system' of democracy, where the voting machines' source code is opened for inspection by political parties, universities, and the Armed Forces before each election, reinforcing public trust in the electoral process.

item.title: Uma ‘batalha antiga’ entre Lula e Flávio volta com força, e deve mexer com as pesquisas
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential election is shaped by a renewed 'old battle' between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro over the religious vote, particularly among Catholics and evangelicals. Flávio Bolsonaro is actively courting evangelicals through frequent church visits and biblical references, while Lula faces declining support in this group, with over 60% rejection among evangelicals driven by influential right-wing religious leaders like Silas Malafaia. Although Lula still holds a significant lead among Catholics, recent surveys show erosion in this traditionally PT-aligned base, prompting analysts to urge the government to defend its Catholic voter bloc amid a highly polarized and tight race.

item.title: Hugo Motta diz que espera que veto de Lula ao PL da Dosimetria seja derrubado
item.description: Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies Hugo Motta expressed hope that Congress will overturn President Lula's veto on the Dosimetry Bill, which would reduce sentences for crimes related to January 8, including Jair Bolsonaro's sentence from 27 years and 3 months to 20 years. He argues the measure could ease tensions between branches by correcting what legislators see as excessive penalties. Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has scheduled the veto vote for the 30th.

item.title: Acórdão do julgamento de Castro no TSE é concluído e não estipula se eleição para mandato-tampão no Rio será direta ou indireta
item.description: The TSE's ruling that made Claudio Castro ineligible has been finalized but does not specify whether the interim mandate election in Rio will be direct or indirect, pending STF decision. Castro resigned before the ruling, which opponents claim was a maneuver to avoid disqualification. The STF awaits the acórdão's publication to resume judging the election format.

item.title: Oscar Schmidt queria ser presidente, tentou vaga no Senado e foi Secretário de Esporte
item.description: Oscar Schmidt, Brazil's basketball idol, died at 68 in São Paulo. Before his death, he ventured into politics in the 1990s, serving as Municipal Secretary of Sports in São Paulo (1997-1998) and running for Senate in 1998, where he lost to Eduardo Suplicy. He stated his Senate bid was part of a larger ambition to become President of Brazil.

item.title: Kassio vota por derrubar lei da Bahia que pune desinformação sobre pandemias
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques voted to strike down a Bahia law that penalizes the spread of false information about pandemics, epidemics, or endemics with fines up to R$20,000. He argued the law overstepped state authority by encroaching on federal powers, particularly by sanctioning telecom concessionaires, and violated freedom of expression. The judgment is taking place in the STF’s virtual plenary until April 28, with opposing views from the AGU and PGR.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro supera Lula em engajamento no Instagram, aponta levantamento
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro surpassed Lula in Instagram engagement in March, recording 24.1 million interactions — 2.56 times more than the president. He posted more (128 vs 105) and achieved a 2.1x higher average engagement per post (188,413 vs 89,607), with nine of the top ten most engaging posts belonging to him. Despite this, polls show Lula leading in the first round.

item.title: Deltan doa sobra de R$ 730 mil arrecadado em vaquinha para indenizar Lula
item.description: Former prosecutor Deltan Dallagnol donated R$ 730,000 to Erastinho Hospital in Curitiba, representing the surplus from donations collected to pay a R$ 146,000 moral damages indemnity to President Lula, following a court decision upheld by the STF. He noted the funds came from over 12,000 Pix donations ranging from R$ 5 to R$ 1,000, with an additional R$ 5,000 from his own pocket. Dallagnol praised donors as 'true heroes' and said directing the surplus to the hospital was a way to 'defeat evil with good'.

item.title: Juiz vê ‘perseguição política’ contra Erika Hilton e rejeita ação de ONG
item.description: Judge Giordano Resende Costa of the 4th Civil Court of Brasília dismissed a public civil action filed by NGO Matria against federal deputy Erika Hilton (PSOL-SP), citing a 'clear bias of political persecution' and protecting her under parliamentary immunity. The suit sought a retraction over Hilton’s social media post criticizing 'transphobes and imbeCIS', a play on 'cis' referring to cisgender individuals opposing trans women’s recognition. The judge stated the NGO aims to silence a lawmaker through judicial means, transforming legitimate ideological disagreement into a punitive R$500,000 claim.

item.title: Ricardo Couto deve ficar no governo até o fim do ano
item.description: The STF has maintained an injunction freezing the succession of the Rio de Janeiro state government, keeping Judge Ricardo Couto in office until the end of the year to avoid holding two costly elections. The decision awaits a plenary ruling and the TSE’s final decision on Claudio Castro’s cassation. Eduardo Paes’ group lost the legislative election, reflecting Castro’s control over the state apparatus.

item.title: Motta diz que apoia derrubada de vetos de Lula ao projeto da redução de penas do 8/1
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) expressed support for overturning President Lula's veto on a bill reducing sentences for those convicted of coup d'état. The measure could benefit former President Jair Bolsonaro (PL), currently under house arrest. The statement was made on Friday, April 17, 2026.

item.title: Pacote de renegociação está pronto e será para 3 grupos, diz Durigan
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan announced that the debt renegotiation package is ready and will target three groups: families, informal workers, and small businesses. The program will not use public funds or subsidize interest rates or terms, with the government acting only as a guarantor. The target audience includes individuals earning up to two minimum wages (or up to five for some modalities) registered in CadÚnico, with discounts of up to 90% and monthly interest rates between 2% and 2.5%.

item.title: Motta quer derrubar veto de Lula à redução das penas de golpistas
item.description: Hugo Motta, President of the Chamber of Deputies, advocated for overturning President Lula’s veto of the Dosimetry Bill, which reduces sentences for those involved in the January 8, 2023 attacks. Senator Davi Alcolumbre scheduled the vote to restore the bill’s validity for April 30, requiring an absolute majority in Congress. Motta stated there was a consensus among technicians and political actors to prevent a new institutional crisis.

item.title: STF forma maioria para manter cassação de Rodrigo Bacellar
item.description: The First Chamber of the STF formed a majority to deny the appeal by Rodrigo Bacellar's defense, upholding the cancellation of his mandate and ineligibility imposed by the TSE. The decision rejected the request to suspend the effects of the electoral ruling that removed him from office.

item.title: Fim da 6 X 1 pode custar R$ 11,88 bi ao setor de transporte, diz CNT
item.description: The CNT warns that ending the 6x1 work schedule in the transport sector could add R$11.9 billion to R$28.1 billion annually in labor costs, potentially leading to the layoff of 42,000 to 84,000 workers and a 1.3% decline in the sector’s GDP. The Lula government proposes an immediate shift to a 40-hour workweek with maintained pay and two days off, claiming productivity gains will offset the costs.

item.title: CDHU fez mais de 10 mil atendimentos individuais a moradores da Favela do Moinho
item.description: The São Paulo government conducted over 10,000 individual consultations in Favela do Moinho over one year, averaging 12 approaches per family, resulting in 916 completed changes. The initiative aims to secure defined and safe housing for residents, with 850 families already guaranteed access to definitive housing through direct purchase or programs like Casa Paulista. The Tarcísio de Freitas administration assesses that the project will enable community disengagement from a high-risk area.

item.title: Maioria do STF nega recurso de Rodrigo Bacellar contra cassação
item.description: The First Chamber of the Supreme Federal Court formed a majority to deny Rodrigo Bacellar's appeal against the cassation of his mandate for abuse of political and economic power. Justice Cristiano Zanin, the rapporteur, upheld the precautionary measure, supported by ministers Flávio Dino and Alexandre de Moraes. The ruling confirms Bacellar's ineligibility for the 2026 elections.

item.title: As estratégias do novo presidente da Alerj para assumir o governo do Rio
item.description: Deputy Douglas Ruas (PL), elected president of the Alerj after two contested votes, is using the position as a stepping stone to assume the governorship of Rio de Janeiro, given the current absence of a governor and vice-governor. Despite judicial challenges from the opposition, Ruas has shifted his tone, accusing them of boycotting the election and causing institutional instability. His strategy includes negotiating with Justice Ricardo Couto, the STF-appointed intervener, and pursuing legal avenues through the Assembly’s legal department to validate his claim to the Guanabara Palace.

item.title: Motta diz que governo avaliou mal projeto sobre aplicativos; Lula volta a defender regulamentação
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta criticized the Lula government for misjudging the bill regulating app-based workers, claiming its withdrawal from the agenda was a mistake that could raise service prices and harm workers. Lula, speaking in Spain, reaffirmed his support for regulation, stressing the need to balance worker autonomy with social protection, decent income, and access to benefits. The issue was postponed due to lack of consensus, as stated by Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães, following a meeting between Lula and Motta in which the Executive concluded it was not the right time to vote on the matter.

item.title: Roberto Reis na Crusoé: A última rodada
item.description: The article suggests that if President Lula acknowledges a growing and possibly irreversible rejection in the next 100 days, he may choose not to run for re-election in 2026 as a rational way to conclude his political career — not out of defeat, but as a dignified and strategic exit.

item.title: Programa de renegociação de dívidas está pronto para ser anunciado após volta de Lula ao Brasil, diz Durigan
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that the federal government's debt renegotiation program is ready and will be announced after President Lula's return to Brazil. The program will use Treasury guarantees to encourage banks to offer better terms to debtors, without affecting the Union's primary spending.

item.title: EUA avisam Brasil que pretendem classificar CV e PCC como terroristas, diz site
item.description: The United States informed Brazil's Central Bank president, Gabriel Galípolo, of its intent to designate the Comando Vermelho (CV) and Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) as terrorist organizations to financially strangle them. The move, driven by lobbying from Jair Bolsonaro's sons — particularly Flávio Bolsonaro, a 2026 presidential pre-candidate — is seen as a potential boost to his campaign, given that public security is a top voter concern in Brazil. Despite opposition from the Lula administration, the U.S. framed the advance notice as a 'deference' to Brazil, unlike designations in Mexico or Venezuela made without prior consultation.

item.title: Governo admite transição para fim da escala 6x1, mas descarta desoneração
item.description: The government admits the possibility of including a transition period for ending the 6x1 work schedule, but ruled out new tax breaks to compensate employers. Minister José Guimarães said President Lula plans to announce the reduction of the workweek from 44 to 40 hours in May, Workers' Month. Furthermore, the bill regulating app-based work will be voted on only after the elections due to lack of consensus among platforms, workers, and the opposition.

item.title: Vai à sanção mais rigor para preso que mantiver ameaças contra mulher
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved Bill 2.083/2022, which provides for the application of the Disciplinary Differentiated Regime (RDD) to inmates convicted of domestic violence against women who continue to threaten or commit violence against the victim or her family, even while incarcerated. The bill includes compulsory transfer to prisons in other states, restrictions on visits, sunbathing, and correspondence, as well as monitoring of interviews, for up to two years. It also amends the Torture Crimes Law to classify repeated subjection of a woman to intense physical or mental suffering in domestic violence contexts as torture, without prejudice to other criminal penalties.

item.title: Crusoé: Ninguém quer Lula como mediador
item.description: President Lula stated he was ignored by world leaders when proposing a UN Security Council meeting to address the war in Iran. In an interview with Der Spiegel, he said he presented the idea to Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Emmanuel Macron, but received no support. The proposal was ultimately dismissed by the interlocutors.

item.title: Tarcísio participou de jantar com empresário do funk preso pela PF
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) attended a dinner on August 12, 2025, with Rodrigo Inácio de Lima Oliveira, a funk businessman arrested by the Federal Police on April 15, 2026, in Operation Narco Fluxo, which investiges a suspected money laundering scheme linked to the PCC involving cryptoassets and over R$1.6 billion. Oliveira, suspected of intermediating artists to conceal drug trafficking proceeds, posted photos with the governor on social media at the time. The operation led to the arrests of MC Ryan, MC Poze do Rodo, and Raphael Sousa Oliveira (creator of the Choquei profile), involving over 200 federal police officers.

item.title: Assessor de Marçal que deu soco em marqueteiro grava vídeo com Flávio
item.description: Nahuel Medina, an aide to candidate Pablo Marçal who punched publicist Duda Lima during the 2024 São Paulo mayoral debate, posted a video alongside Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The video was published on Thursday, April 16, 2026, amid the 2026 election campaign. The gesture highlights alliances between far-right factions and Bolsonaro-linked figures.

item.title: 'Queremos que a escala 6x1 acabe já', diz Boulos sobre projeto de Lula
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos said he wants an immediate end to the 6x1 work scale proposed by the Lula government, advocating for a 90-day transition period for companies to adapt, rejecting the five-year timeline suggested in the CCJ as 'postponement'. He also discussed the bill regulating app-based work, defending a minimum payment of R$10 per trip as a fair inflation-adjusted reimbursement for motorcycle couriers.

item.title: Tarcísio nega que saída de ex-chefe da PM foi motivada por citação em investigação da Corregedoria
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas denied that the change in command of São Paulo’s Military Police was motivated by the mention of former chief Coronel José Augusto Coutinho in a Corregedoria investigation into alleged links with the PCC and the Transwolff bus company. He stated Coutinho requested to leave for personal reasons and praised his impeccable record, noting such rotations are common and that the new commander, Coronel Glauce Anselmo Cavalli, was selected for her distinguished career. Coutinho’s defense claims he has not accessed the investigation files and reiterates his integrity, while the São Paulo government refuses to comment on ongoing Corregedoria proceedings due to legal secrecy.

item.title: Após vitória na Alerj, Douglas Ruas diz que falará com Ricardo Couto e STF sobre linha sucessória no estado
item.description: Douglas Ruas, elected president of the Alerj by the PL, announced he will inform acting governor Ricardo Couto and the STF of his victory to discuss the state's succession line. He stated that, if he assumes command, he intends to build upon and improve measures taken by the current president of the TJ-RJ, describing the situation as 'totally atypical'. His election has raised questions about judicialization to secure the succession, with the PL already filing a request with the STF.

item.title: Declaração de Motta sobre veto ao PL da Dosimetria preocupa governistas
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta said he hopes President Lula’s full veto of the Dosimetria bill will be overturned by Congress, arguing the proposal aims to ease tensions between the Legislative and Judicial branches, particularly regarding sentences related to the January 8 events. A session to review the veto has been scheduled for April 30 by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. Government allies are concerned Motta may personally rally to overturn the veto, though Centrist lawmakers believe the vote margin will be narrow.

item.title: Fim da taxa das blusinhas divide integrantes do governo Lula
item.description: Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães expressed support for repealing the 'blusinhas' tax, acknowledging it harms President Lula’s popularity. Vice President Geraldo Alckmin countered that no government decision has been made, defending the 20% levy on international purchases under $50, arguing total import taxes remain lower than those on domestic production. The issue exposes a rift in the Lula administration, with economic officials backing the tax and political allies pushing for its removal.

item.title: Zanin e Moraes votam para manter cassação de Rodrigo Bacellar
item.description: Minister Cristiano Zanin voted to deny a legal appeal by the defense of former state deputy Rodrigo Bacellar (União-RJ), upholding the TSE's decision that revoked his mandate and declared him ineligible. The First Chamber of the STF followed Zanin's vote, confirming the rejection of the request to suspend the effects of the removal.

item.title: Vídeo: Senado Aprova: Regulamentação dos percentuais mínimos de cacau em seus derivados
item.description: The Senate approved PL 1.769/2019, which sets minimum cacao percentages in cocoa-derived products such as chocolate and cocoa powder, requiring labels, packaging, and advertising to disclose the total cacao content. Non-compliant companies will face sanctions under the Consumer Defense Code and sanitary legislation. The bill now awaits presidential sanction. Additionally, the Senate approved the nomination of Deputy Odair Cunha (PT-MG) for a ministerial position at the TCU (Federal Court of Accounts), with 50 votes in favor and 8 against, to fill the vacancy left by retired Minister Aroldo Cedraz. The TCU oversees the president’s annual accounts and monitors federal public spending.

item.title: O Preço do Futuro (Parte 1)
item.description: Prediction markets offer a real-time mechanism to gauge expectations about future events — such as elections, interest rates, and inflation — by converting probabilities into tradable contract prices. In the Brazilian context, these markets could reveal market confidence in the Copom’s decisions, inflation trajectory, political risk, and international credibility, especially amid global volatility. Extending this logic to Brazilian politics would enable precise tracking of informed bets on electoral outcomes and policy shifts, turning news into market conviction signals.

item.title: ‘Médico dos presidentes’, Roberto Kalil Filho é eleito membro titular da Academia Nacional de Medicina
item.description: Cardiologist Roberto Kalil Filho, known as the "doctor of presidents," was elected a titular member of the National Academy of Medicine with 72 out of 96 votes, occupying Chair No. 01. He emphasized the institution's relevance to society and noted his role as physician to President Lula. His career includes over 300 scientific publications and leadership roles at FMUSP, Sírio-Libanês, and InCor.

item.title: Moraes vota por condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro a um ano de detenção por difamar Tabata
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes voted to convict Eduardo Bolsonaro to one year of detention in an open regime and 39 days-fine for defamation against Deputy Tabata Amaral. Moraes stated that Bolsonaro falsely accused Tabata of intending to illicitly benefit third parties through her bill on public distribution of sanitary pads, acting with full awareness of the offensive nature of his posts. The vote was delivered in the STF’s virtual plenary, with the session set to conclude on April 28.

item.title: Lula fala em regulação digital para barrar interferência externa em ano eleitoral
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advocated for digital regulation to prevent foreign interference in Brazil's 2026 elections, speaking a day before a meeting with other progressive leaders. He also offered self-criticism regarding the global rise of extremism, emphasizing threats to democracy.

item.title: Fachin critica relatório da CPI que mirava ministros do STF, mas nega crise institucional com Senado
item.description: Supreme Federal Court President Edson Fachin criticized the Senate Organized Crime CPI report calling for the impeachment of STF ministers and the Attorney General, arguing judicial decisions should be challenged through appeals, not institutional attacks. He denied an institutional crisis between the Judiciary and Legislature, stating there are only interpretive disagreements on the scope of CPIs, and stressed that both branches must uphold their prerogatives while subjecting parliamentary work to public scrutiny.
